summary.text: Thomas Melville is the Democratic candidate for the Massachusetts House of Representatives, 9th Norfolk District, in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A licensed attorney and former news executive, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that he began his career as a Peace Corps volunteer and later led newsrooms at NECN and WBUR.

paragraphs.text: Melville graduated from Newton South High School, earned a bachelor's degree from Boston University in 1980 and a law degree from Boston College Law School in 1986, according to Ballotpedia.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said his career began as a U.S. Peace Corps volunteer in the Dominican Republic, followed by work as a television news anchor and reporter, news director at New England Cable News and executive news director at WBUR, and later communications director at the MIT Energy Initiative.
He also said he received journalism awards including a George Foster Peabody Award.
Melville said in the survey that he served as board president of the Medfield Afterschool Program and was a founding member of the Norfolk/Medfield conference of the St. Vincent de Paul Society.
He advanced from the Democratic primary on September 1, 2026.
His stated priorities include increasing state aid for education and infrastructure, holding investor-owned utilities responsible for energy costs, and capping health insurance premiums.
